handoff.goals: Wire client-side PostHog identification to the app’s stable authenticated user identity so browser events and errors inherit it, and clear it on logout.
handoff.did: Updated `src/App.tsx` only. The existing centralized Supabase auth synchronization now imports the initialized `posthog-js` singleton and tracks the previously identified user ID. On an existing session or auth success it calls `posthog.identify(user.id, { email })` exactly once for the Supabase UUID, with email retained solely as a person property. Repeated auth notifications for the same user do not repeat identification. A direct account switch resets before identifying the new UUID; an identified sign-out resets PostHog. Calls are guarded by `posthog.__loaded`, preserving production no-op behavior when PostHog configuration is absent. This establishes identity once at the auth boundary, so all later browser-side captures and PostHog-reported errors inherit it automatically.
handoff.forNextAgent: No per-event distinct-ID tagging is needed for browser PostHog calls: the shared client persists the Supabase UUID identity after authentication. The API has no PostHog server SDK/events per upstream handoff, so no backend request identity wiring was added. Any later browser instrumentation should use the already initialized shared client or `usePostHog()` hook.
handoff.evidence: Re-read `src/App.tsx` after the targeted edit. Verified the identify call uses `user.id` (Supabase’s stable UUID), email appears only in identify person properties, duplicate same-user auth notifications return early, account switches reset before identify, and identified sign-outs reset. Per task instruction, no build, lint, or tests were run.
handoff.assumptions: Supabase `User.id` is the application’s stable authenticated primary key, and the existing `src/main.tsx` initialization runs before this rendered auth effect.

handoff.reportSection:
## Error tracking

Added a global `PostHogErrorBoundary` at the React entry point in `src/main.tsx`. It wraps the rendered application tree and retains the existing `ErrorFallback`, so uncaught React render errors are reported to PostHog Error Tracking without scattering manual exception capture across routes or components.

handoff.goals: Add AI Observability to every production LLM call already made by the application, without changing LLM request behavior or instrumenting developer-only tooling.
handoff.did: Selected `ai-observability-manual-capture`: the production `api/openrouter.ts` call uses raw `fetch` against OpenRouter and the manifest has no vendor LLM SDK, so the OpenRouter wrapper is not applicable. Updated `api/openrouter.ts` to construct a guarded server-only `posthog-node` client from `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `POSTHOG_HOST`, with `privacyMode: false`, serverless-safe batching (`flushAt: 1`, `flushInterval: 0`, 2-second request timeout, no retries), and no exception-autocapture option. The existing OpenRouter request is unchanged; each completed, rejected, or network-failed generation now emits a non-blocking, caught-and-flushed `$ai_generation` event with the authenticated Supabase UUID as `distinctId`, a fresh UUID `$ai_trace_id`, actual request/response content, model, provider, usage, latency, status, and error metadata. This feeds AI Observability generation, latency, token, status, and failure analysis. The AI Task Generator has no multi-turn conversation or tool loop, so `$ai_session_id` is explicitly `null` and no `$ai_span` events were added. Updated `.env.example` to document server-only PostHog configuration names and set the supplied public project token/host in `.env.local` through the env tool. Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-ai.json` so reporting recognizes the OpenRouter/manual-capture setup. The Vite dev-server OpenRouter proxy in `vite.config.js` was inspected but intentionally left untouched as developer-only LLM tooling; the deployed serverless endpoint is the production target. No MCP server or MCP-server LLM calls were detected.
handoff.forNextAgent: Review/install must add `posthog-node` before build/type checking; this task deliberately did not change the dependency manifest, lockfile, run a package manager, import-check, build, app, or paid LLM request. Also configure `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `POSTHOG_HOST` in the production serverless/Vercel environment; `.env.local` only covers local execution. To verify after deployment, sign in, open the Tasks flow’s AI Task Generator, submit one task prompt, then inspect the newest generation under AI Observability > Traces at https://us.posthog.com. Expect one trace containing one `task_generation` generation attributed to the authenticated Supabase UUID; no AI session is expected because each request is one-shot. Delivery is wired but unverified. Privacy mode: effective setting is off (`privacyMode: false`) in `api/openrouter.ts` near the module-level PostHog constructor, so manual capture sends prompt and completion content. Before sending sensitive prompts or outputs, set that option to `true` and update `captureGeneration` in the same file to omit `$ai_input`, `$ai_output_choices`, and any sensitive manual error content; manual capture properties are explicitly supplied and should not rely on an SDK option to redact them. See https://posthog.com/docs/ai-observability/privacy-mode.
handoff.evidence: Re-read `api/openrouter.ts` after editing and confirmed the guarded `posthog-node` client, one `randomUUID()` trace per OpenRouter request, `$ai_generation` capture on success/HTTP failure/network failure, stable authenticated distinct ID, and caught serverless flush. A targeted grep confirmed the import and all three capture call paths. No runtime verification was performed by instruction.

handoff.goals: Configure PostHog Logs capture for the project's supported browser and Node/Vercel API runtimes, using the documented platform integrations while exporting only log lines added in this task.
handoff.did:
- `src/main.tsx`: configured the already-initialized `posthog-js` client with Logs resource identity (`unitracker-web` and the Vite build mode). This enables the browser-native PostHog logger without console autocapture.
- `src/hooks/tasks/useTaskSubmit.ts`: added two structured browser log records, `task created` and `task updated`, only after their existing persistence operations succeed. Their attributes are limited to task configuration booleans and feed Logs queries for task-save outcomes; no identifiers, titles, notes, or other user-entered content are included.
- `api/posthogLogs.ts`: added a dedicated `LoggerProvider`-owned logger (not the global OpenTelemetry Logs API) with an OTLP HTTP exporter that derives its ingestion endpoint and authorization from `POSTHOG_HOST` and `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`. It uses a batch processor, does not delay application startup or request responses, exports only calls made through `logToPostHog`, and attempts a caught flush only at process shutdown.
- `api/openrouter.ts`: added purpose-written structured API logs for OpenRouter generation completion in success, provider-error, and network-error paths. They include only outcome, allowed model, response status where applicable, and duration; request messages, error text, keys, and user identifiers are excluded. These feed operational Logs analysis for AI generation availability and latency.
Existing console output and log handlers remain unchanged and are not exported by this integration.
handoff.forNextAgent: Review/install the listed packages before running type-check or build; this task deliberately did not edit `package.json`/`bun.lock`, install packages, or run validation. The required configuration names are already present from upstream: browser `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST`; server `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `POSTHOG_HOST`. Ensure the server values are configured in Vercel production as well as local development. Delivery is wired but unverified. To verify browser Logs, create or update a task and filter PostHog Logs by service `unitracker-web` for `task created` or `task updated`. To verify API Logs, submit the AI Task Generator and filter service `unitracker-api` for `openrouter generation completed`; inspect `outcome`, `model`, and `duration_ms`. Only records explicitly added by this run are exported. To route existing browser console logging too, add `captureConsoleLogs: true` to the existing `logs` configuration in `src/main.tsx` only after auditing its output; this is intentionally not enabled. For existing API logging, replace a selected safe `console.*` call with `logToPostHog(...)` rather than attaching the exporter to a global logger.
handoff.evidence: Read the React/React Router framework commandments, installed and read the JavaScript and Node.js Logs skills plus their platform references, inspected the existing runtime/logging setup, detected Bun as the preferred package manager, and re-read every changed file after editing. handoff.reportSection:
## Log capture

Configured PostHog Logs for the browser and Node/Vercel API runtimes. Browser task saves emit structured `task created` and `task updated` records under `unitracker-web`; OpenRouter generation completion emits structured success, provider-error, and network-error records under `unitracker-api`. The API exporter is isolated to a dedicated LoggerProvider-owned logger and derives both endpoint and authorization from server environment variables. Only log lines added by this run are exported; existing console output remains local. Install the listed OpenTelemetry packages (and the upstream-required `posthog-node`) before validation. Delivery remains unverified: create or update a task, or run the AI Task Generator, then search Logs at https://us.posthog.com filtered by the appropriate service. To export existing browser console output too, add `captureConsoleLogs: true` to the existing `logs` configuration after a privacy audit.
